requirement: Describe this as a randomized pilot comparing an 8-week Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction program with an active Brain Health control in people with brain injury or stroke.

evidence.text: Participants are randomly assigned to MBSR or an active Brain Health control for the pilot wellness-program comparison.

requirement: Use covariate-adaptive randomization to create equal-sized groups balanced on age, education, stroke side, lesion volume, months post-stroke, MMSE cognitive status, and baseline anxiety and depression.

evidence.text: The protocol lists the covariate-adaptive randomization factors and the goal of equal balanced groups.

requirement: Describe MBSR as weekly 2.5-hour sessions with a 7.5-hour retreat in Week 6 and home practice, and state that Brain Health is matched on hours, instructor, schedule, homework, and home practice without the mindfulness component.

evidence.text: The protocol describes the MBSR schedule and the process-matched Brain Health control.

requirement: Schedule standardized psychological and cognitive testing before intervention and within one week after intervention, performed by a licensed neuropsychologist blinded to treatment condition.

evidence.text: Pre- and post-testing within one week after the intervention is conducted by a licensed neuropsychologist blinded to group.

requirement: Identify reduction from pre- to post-intervention in depression and anxiety, measured by the Geriatric Depression Scale and State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, as the primary Aim 2 outcome target.

evidence.text: The SAP identifies reduced depression and anxiety scores using GDS and STAI as the primary outcome target for Aim 2.

requirement: Identify pre- to post-intervention change in cognitive performance measured by RBANS as the secondary Aim 2 outcome target.

evidence.text: The protocol includes RBANS in the blinded assessment battery.
The SAP identifies change in RBANS cognitive performance as the secondary outcome target.

requirement: Assess recruitment feasibility from counts contacted, willing, and eligible, and define success as recruiting at least 70% of eligible patients from the available pools.
acceptable_values: at least 70% of eligible patients recruited

evidence.text: Recruitment feasibility uses the recruitment flow counts and a minimum 70% recruitment criterion.

requirement: Define retention as completion of all program components and require at least 70% retention separately in both MBSR and Brain Health groups.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies 70% retention in both groups based on completing all program components.

requirement: Evaluate effective participation against all three criteria: every participant attends more than 70% of sessions, averages more than 3 hours of weekly practice or homework, and scores at least 75% correct on the post-test quiz.

evidence.text: The SAP gives three explicit participation thresholds for attendance, home work, and comprehension.

requirement: Assess treatment fidelity from videotaped sessions by having independent clinicians familiar with the programs rate a random sample of four sessions on a 1-to-5 manual-adherence scale.

evidence.text: Fidelity is rated by independent clinicians for four randomly sampled sessions on a 1-5 scale.

requirement: Evaluate assessor blinding at study end with a forced-choice prediction of MBSR versus Brain Health membership plus the assessor's confidence in that prediction.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies a forced-choice group-recognition test and confidence rating for the blinded neuropsychologist.

requirement: Evaluate randomization performance by comparing demographic summary-table values between the MBSR and Brain Health groups.

evidence.text: Randomization procedures are evaluated by comparing group values in demographic summary tables.

requirement: State that this pilot cannot establish definitive intervention safety and require serious adverse events to be brought to Mental Health and reported to the VA IRB within 24 hours.

evidence.text: The SAP limits the pilot safety claim and specifies the 24-hour serious-adverse-event reporting rule.

requirement: Define intervention acceptability as an average of at least 4.0 out of 5 on every questionnaire item and at least 80% of participants rating one or more course components at least 7 out of 10.
acceptable_values: at least one component rated 7 of 10 or higher

evidence.text: The SAP gives both questionnaire-based acceptability thresholds.

requirement: Analyze open-ended participant-experience responses with content-analysis software to identify recurring themes.

evidence.text: Open-ended questionnaire responses are to be analyzed with content-analysis software to identify common themes.

requirement: Use descriptive statistics for the pilot outcome analyses and do not present inferential treatment-effect testing as the prespecified primary analysis.

evidence.text: The SAP says inferential treatment-effect statistics are not appropriate for the pilot and that descriptive statistics will be reported.

notes: This distinction is central to preventing the future-study example from being misrepresented as the active pilot analysis.

requirement: Label the group-by-time mixed random-effects model as a reference for a subsequent efficacy study only, and request confirmation of the pilot sample size, analysis populations, exact descriptive summaries, missing-data handling, and any formal outcome hierarchy before specifying them as final pilot methods.
acceptable_values: do not invent inferential pilot methods

evidence.text: The mixed random-effects model is introduced only as the type of analysis for a subsequent efficacy study; the concise pilot plan omits the other requested details.

notes: If mentioned, the illustrative future model has treatment, time, and interaction fixed effects, includes participants with baseline and at least one post-intervention session, assumes ignorable attrition, and is not ITT; none of those choices should be activated for this pilot without confirmation.
